time: About 45 minutes, plus 20 minutes to soak cashews
basis: The page describes a tomato-chipotle tinga with crumbled tofu and black beans, cabbage slaw, and cashew crema. Its ingredient list also includes cumin, nutritional yeast, lemon, and red onion.

Tinga filling: 14 oz (400 g) extra-firm tofu, drained and pressed for 15 minutes
1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
1 can (14–15 oz) crushed or finely chopped tomatoes
1–2 chipotle peppers in adobo, minced, plus 1 tsp adobo sauce
½ tsp fine salt to start
Cashew crema: ½ cup raw cashews, soaked in hot water 20 minutes and drained
⅓ cup fresh water, plus more to thin

steps: Blend the drained cashews with fresh water, citrus juices, nutritional yeast, garlic powder, and salt until completely smooth. Add water a tablespoon at a time until it drizzles easily.
Toss cabbage, red onion, cilantro, lime juice, and salt. Let stand while cooking the filling; drain excess liquid before assembling.
Heat olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5–7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, tomato paste, chipotle, cumin, paprika, and oregano; stir for 1 minute.

Crumble the tofu into roughly pea-size pieces. Add it with tomatoes, beans, bay leaf, and ½ tsp salt. Simmer uncovered for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick enough to sit in a tortilla without dripping. Add a splash of water if it dries before the flavors come together. Remove the bay leaf and adjust salt and heat.
Warm tortillas in a dry skillet for 20–30 seconds per side. Divide filling among 8 tortillas, add drained slaw, and drizzle with crema. Serve with lime wedges.
notes: The page gives no component quantities. Start with one chipotle for moderate heat; the second makes the filling hotter. These servings are not matched to the delivered meal’s portion or nutrition.
reheat: For the delivered meal: separate sauce, slaw, lime, and tortillas. Heat filling at 350°F for 10–15 minutes, or microwave about 2 minutes until hot. Microwave tortillas about 20 seconds, then assemble with the cold toppings.

short: Quinoa & veggie enchiladas with rice and beans
yield_: 4 servings · 8 enchiladas, plus rice and beans
basis: The description names quinoa, kale, Oaxaca/Monterey Jack cheese, chipotle cream, and rice with black beans. The label additionally lists poblano, jalapeño, corn, cream cheese, pepper jack, cheddar, cotija, tomatoes, and other seasonings.

Enchiladas: 1 tbsp olive oil, plus a little for the baking dish
½ jalapeño, minced; remove seeds for less heat
2 cups finely chopped kale, tough stems removed
¼ tsp fine salt, then more to taste
Chipotle cream and topping: ¾ cup canned diced tomatoes with juice
1 chipotle pepper in adobo, plus 1 tsp adobo sauce
Rice and beans: ½ cup dry basmati rice, rinsed
1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed

steps: Heat oven to 375°F and lightly oil a baking dish. Simmer quinoa with 1 cup water, covered, for about 15 minutes until absorbed. Take off heat and rest covered 5 minutes.

For the rice, heat 1 tbsp oil in a saucepan. Soften onion and red pepper for 5–7 minutes. Add garlic, cumin, and oregano; stir 30 seconds. Add plum tomato and cook 2 minutes. Stir in rice, broth, and bay leaf. Cover and simmer on low for 12–15 minutes, or according to the rice package. Fold in drained beans, cover, and warm on low 3–5 minutes; add a splash of water if needed. Rest off heat 5 minutes. Remove bay leaf; add lemon and salt to taste.

For the filling, heat 1 tbsp oil in a skillet. Cook onion, poblano, and jalapeño for 6–8 minutes. Add garlic for 30 seconds, then kale and corn. Cook 3–4 minutes until kale softens and excess moisture evaporates. Off heat, stir in quinoa, cream cheese, Oaxaca, pepper jack, and ¼ tsp salt.
Blend cream, canned tomatoes, chipotle, adobo, cumin, and salt. Pour into a small saucepan and gently simmer for 5 minutes, stirring. Avoid a vigorous boil.

Warm corn tortillas in a covered damp towel in the microwave for 30–45 seconds, until pliable. Spread a little sauce in the baking dish. Divide filling among tortillas, roll, and set seam-side down. Spoon remaining sauce over them and scatter cheddar on top.
Cover and bake for 15 minutes, then uncover for 5–10 minutes until bubbling at the edges. Finish with cotija and cilantro. Serve two enchiladas per person with rice and beans.
notes: The page refers to multiple sauce cups without identifying their separate formulas. This reconstruction uses one chipotle cream. Pepper jack follows the ingredient label; Monterey Jack is named in the description. The home version simplifies commercial oil blends and seasoning additives.
reheat: For the delivered meal: remove sauce cups and packaging film. Oven: 350°F for 12–15 minutes. Microwave: vent film and heat 2–3 minutes. Add sauces afterward.

short: Vegan vodka rigatoni with eggplant meatballs
basis: The page describes rigatoni, tomato and roasted-red-pepper vodka sauce with cashew cream, and eggplant meatballs containing pumpkin and lentils. Spinach, panko, and nutritional yeast appear in the label.

Eggplant meatballs: 1 medium-large eggplant, about 1 lb (450 g), cut into ¾-inch cubes
¾ cup cooked green lentils, well drained
¾ cup panko, plus up to ¼ cup more if needed
¼ tsp each garlic powder and onion powder
Vodka sauce: ½ cup raw cashews, soaked in hot water 20 minutes and drained
½ cup drained roasted red peppers
¼ tsp crushed red pepper, or to taste
½ tsp fine salt, then more to taste
1 tsp coconut sugar, optional if tomatoes taste sharp

steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss eggplant with 1½ tbsp oil, spread on a baking sheet, and roast 25–30 minutes, turning once, until very soft and browned. Let cool enough to handle. Reduce oven to 400°F.

Heat remaining ½ tbsp meatball oil in a skillet. Soften the half onion for 5 minutes, then cook garlic 30 seconds. Pulse this mixture with roasted eggplant and lentils in a food processor until coarsely chopped, not smooth.

Fold in pumpkin, panko, nutritional yeast, parsley, oregano, powders, salt, and pepper. Rest 10 minutes so crumbs hydrate. The mixture should hold a ball when gently squeezed; add extra panko a tablespoon at a time if too wet. Form about 16 balls on a parchment-lined sheet. Bake 25–30 minutes at 400°F until firm and browned; turn carefully after 18 minutes. Let set on the tray for 5 minutes.

Meanwhile, blend drained cashews with ¾ cup fresh water until silky. In a wide saucepan, heat 1 tbsp oil and cook sauce onion for 5 minutes. Add garlic and tomato paste; cook 1–2 minutes. Take pan off the burner before adding measured vodka, then return to medium heat and simmer for 2–3 minutes.

Add tomatoes, roasted peppers, bay leaf, crushed red pepper, and salt. Simmer uncovered 20 minutes, stirring. Remove bay leaf, blend until smooth with an immersion blender, and stir in cashew cream and nutritional yeast. Gently simmer 3–5 minutes. Taste before adding optional sugar.

Boil rigatoni in salted water according to the package until al dente, reserving 1 cup pasta water. Toss pasta and spinach into the sauce over low heat until spinach wilts, adding pasta water as needed. Plate with meatballs on top, then basil and chives. Avoid simmering the soft meatballs in the sauce.
notes: Pumpkin and lentils help bind the eggplant, but moisture varies; the panko adjustment is an estimated home technique. This recipe has not been kitchen-tested. The listed vodka can be omitted and replaced with water for a different, alcohol-free sauce.
reheat: For the delivered meal: chop the spinach and stir it into the pasta. Heat without film at 350°F for 8–10 minutes, or microwave with vented film for about 2 minutes, until hot.

basis: The page names vegan chorizo-and-bean chili, vegan cheddar, gluten-free tortillas, pico de gallo, and chile-lime crema. The ingredient list includes both Impossible meat and vegan chorizo, as well as vegan Parmesan.

Chili and quesadillas: 4 large brown-rice or other gluten-free tortillas
¾ cup cooked black beans, drained
Salt and black pepper to taste
Pico de gallo: ¼ serrano pepper, minced, optional for more heat

steps: Combine pico ingredients and set aside. Stir together crema ingredients, thinning with water if needed. Keep both cool while cooking.

Heat 2 tsp oil in a skillet over medium heat. Soften onion for 5 minutes. Add plant-based ground meat and chorizo; crumble and cook according to their package directions until cooked through and browned. Add garlic, tomato paste, chipotle, cumin, and oregano; stir 1 minute.

Add beans and crushed tomatoes. Simmer uncovered for 8–12 minutes until very thick. Mash a few beans to help bind the filling. Taste before adding salt, since the meat substitutes and cheese are seasoned. Let cool 5 minutes.
Warm tortillas briefly so they bend without splitting. Divide cheddar, chili, and Parmesan over one half of each tortilla, leaving a ½-inch border; fold closed.

Wipe the skillet and lightly brush with remaining oil. Cook quesadillas in batches over medium-low heat for about 3–4 minutes per side until crisp and the cheese melts. A lid for the first 1–2 minutes helps melt vegan cheese; uncover to finish crisping.
Rest 2 minutes before cutting. Serve with drained pico and chile-lime crema on the side.
notes: Choose gluten-free tortillas and check the meat substitutes if you want the home version to follow the page’s “No Gluten Added” specification. Component proportions are estimated; the source does not state the ratio of its two meat substitutes.
reheat: For the delivered meal: set both sauces aside. Put quesadilla on a baking sheet at 350°F for 13–15 minutes. Alternatively microwave in its vented container for 3–4 minutes, adding 30-second intervals as needed. Serve with the reserved cold sauces.

basis: The description explicitly says the sauce combines equal parts marinara and Alfredo, with crushed red pepper, grana cheese, and basil. The ingredient label lists American Grana, although the meal title says Grana Padano.

Pasta: ¼ cup grated Grana Padano or American Grana, for serving
Marinara: ½ tsp crushed red pepper, or to taste
Alfredo-style sauce: ½ cup finely grated Grana Padano or American Grana

steps: Put a large pot of salted water on to boil. For marinara, heat oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Soften onion for 5–6 minutes; add garlic and red pepper and stir 30 seconds. Add tomatoes and salt, then simmer uncovered 15–20 minutes. Stir in basil. Add sugar only if the sauce tastes too acidic.

For the white sauce, melt butter over medium-low heat in a second saucepan. Cook shallot 3–4 minutes without browning. Add garlic for 30 seconds, then cream. Simmer gently for 3–5 minutes until slightly thickened. Remove from heat and gradually stir in ½ cup grated cheese and black pepper.

Measure equal volumes of red and white sauce into a wide skillet, starting with 1¼ cups of each. If one sauce yields less, use that amount of each; reserve any excess separately. This preserves the page’s stated equal-parts approach despite variation in evaporation.

Cook penne until al dente according to its package. Reserve 1 cup pasta water before draining. Toss pasta with the combined sauce over low heat for 1–2 minutes, adding pasta water a little at a time until glossy and loose enough to coat each piece. Avoid boiling hard after the cheese goes in.
Taste and adjust salt and chili. Divide among bowls, then finish with the reserved ¼ cup cheese and fresh basil.
notes: Equal red/white sauce proportions are stated by CookUnity; ingredient amounts and sauce preparation here are estimated. If vegetarian rennet matters to you, select a grana-style cheese explicitly labeled accordingly.
reheat: For the delivered meal: keep the cheese cup aside. Cover with foil and heat at 350°F for 12–15 minutes, stirring halfway. Or microwave with vented film for 2–3 minutes, stirring halfway. Add cheese after heating.

short: Hearts of palm quinoa salad with cucumber dressing
basis: The page describes ponzu-marinated quinoa, hearts of palm, tomatoes, cucumber, crisp fried quinoa, and cucumber-tofu dressing. The label also includes edamame, black beans, vegan feta, lettuce, mint, yuzu, kombu, and shiitake.

Salad: ¾ cup dry tri-color quinoa, rinsed
1½ cups water
1 can (14 oz) hearts of palm, drained and sliced
1 cup shelled edamame, cooked according to package and cooled
1 cup canned black beans, drained and rinsed
1 cup halved cherry tomatoes
1 cup diced cucumber
2 cups shredded iceberg lettuce
½ cup crumbled vegan feta
2 tbsp chopped mint
Estimated vegan ponzu: 1 small piece kombu, about 2 inches square
2 tbsp yuzu juice; lemon juice is a home substitution
Cucumber-tofu dressing: Salt and black pepper to taste
Crisp quinoa topping: ½ cup of the cooked quinoa above
2 tsp neutral oil (home addition; the page does not identify a frying oil)

steps: Cook quinoa with 1½ cups water: bring to a boil, cover, and simmer gently about 15 minutes until absorbed. Rest off heat, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff, reserve ½ cup for the topping, and spread the rest on a tray to cool.

For ponzu, soak shiitake and kombu in ¼ cup hot water for 15 minutes. Remove solids. Combine infused water and mirin in a small saucepan; simmer 2 minutes. Cool, then add soy sauce, yuzu, and rice vinegar. This is an estimated shortcut, not the chef’s published formula.

Pat the reserved ½ cup cooked quinoa very dry on paper towels. Warm 2 tsp oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Spread quinoa in a thin layer and cook, stirring periodically, for 8–12 minutes until dry and crisp. Lower heat if it browns too quickly. Cool on a plate.

Blend tofu, dressing cucumber, vegan mayonnaise, white vinegar, mustard, garlic, mint, and cumin until smooth. Taste and add salt and pepper. If thin from a watery cucumber, chill before using; if too thick, add water a teaspoon at a time.
Toss the cooled salad quinoa with 3 tbsp ponzu to start. Add more to taste, a tablespoon at a time, stopping before it becomes wet or overly salty; reserve any remaining ponzu.

Arrange lettuce in four bowls. Divide quinoa, hearts of palm, edamame, black beans, tomatoes, and diced cucumber among them. Add feta and mint, drizzle with cucumber dressing, and add crisp quinoa just before eating.
notes: The source does not assign every seasoning to a component. Ponzu, dressing ratios, and the skillet method for crisp quinoa are reconstructions. The listed soy sauce contains wheat. Lemon in place of yuzu and oil for the topping are explicitly identified home choices.
reheat: The delivered salad is intended to be served chilled: remove packaging and the sauce cup, then add dressing. The page gives no heating step.

short: Mexican tofu burrito bowl with avocado sauce
time: About 50 minutes, plus 15 minutes to press tofu
basis: The description names baked seasoned tofu, roasted peppers and corn, rice, black beans, and creamy avocado sauce. The label includes lemon juice, brown sugar, sriracha, cornstarch, chili powder, garlic powder, and onion powder.

Tofu: 14 oz (400 g) extra-firm tofu, drained and pressed 15 minutes
Rice, beans, and vegetables: ¾ cup dry basmati rice, rinsed
1½ cups water, or amount specified by the rice package
1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
Avocado sauce: ¼ cup water, plus more to thin

steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Cut pressed tofu into ¾-inch cubes and pat dry. Toss with 1 tbsp oil, cornstarch, chili powder, garlic powder, onion powder, and ½ tsp salt. Spread on a parchment-lined sheet with space between pieces.

Toss peppers and corn with their oil and ¼ tsp salt on a separate sheet. Roast tofu for 25–30 minutes, turning halfway; roast vegetables for 20–25 minutes, stirring once, until tender with browned edges.
Meanwhile, cook rice with its water according to package directions. Rest covered 5 minutes, then fluff. Warm beans in a small saucepan with 2 tbsp water for 4–5 minutes and drain excess liquid.
Mix sriracha, brown sugar, and 1 tbsp lemon juice. Toss the browned tofu with this glaze and return to the oven for 3–5 minutes, just until it clings. Watch closely so the sugar does not burn.
Blend avocado with 2 tbsp lemon juice, ¼ cup water, cilantro, garlic powder, and salt until creamy. Add water a tablespoon at a time until spoonable.
Divide rice and beans among four bowls; add roasted vegetables and tofu. Finish with cilantro and avocado sauce.
notes: The glaze is inferred from the listed sriracha, sugar, and lemon; the page does not say how they are used. Lemon follows the ingredient label. Quantities are estimated and do not reproduce the published packaged-meal nutrition.
reheat: For the delivered meal: reserve the sauce. Heat at 350°F for 12–15 minutes with film removed, or microwave with vented film for 2–3 minutes. Add avocado sauce after heating.

time: About 65 minutes using dry lentils; about 40 with cooked lentils
basis: The page describes lentils simmered in a tomato-pepper sauce, fettuccine, feta, and parsley. The ingredient label includes brown lentils, red pepper, white wine, paprika, oregano, and bay leaf.

Lentil sauce: ¾ cup dry brown lentils, rinsed and checked, or about 2 cups cooked lentils
3 cups water for cooking dry lentils, plus more if needed
½ tsp fine salt, then more to taste
½–1 cup water as needed for the sauce

steps: If using dry lentils, place them in a saucepan with 3 cups water. Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 20–30 minutes until tender but intact, adding water to keep them submerged. Drain. If using cooked lentils, drain and proceed.
Heat oil in a wide, deep skillet over medium heat. Cook onion and red pepper for 8–10 minutes until softened. Add garlic, tomato paste, paprika, oregano, and chili powder; stir for 1–2 minutes.

Pour in wine and simmer 2–3 minutes, scraping the bottom. Add tomatoes, cooked lentils, bay leaf, salt, pepper, and ½ cup water. Simmer uncovered for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and spoon-coating. Add more water if needed to prevent sticking.
Mash roughly one quarter of the lentils against the pan with a spoon for a thicker texture, leaving most intact. Remove bay leaf and taste for salt.

Cook fettuccine in salted water according to package directions. Reserve 1 cup pasta water, then drain. Toss pasta with the sauce over low heat, adding pasta water in small splashes until it coats the noodles evenly.
Divide among bowls and finish with feta and parsley.
notes: The page’s description calls this vegan, but its label explicitly lists dairy feta and milk as an allergen, and its specification says vegetarian. This reconstruction uses dairy feta to follow the label. To make a vegan adaptation, use vegan feta and confirm the pasta and wine suit that preference.

short: Superfood bowl with sweet potato, quinoa & black beans
time: About 45 minutes, plus cooling if serving chilled
basis: The page describes sweet potato, quinoa, black beans, herbs, and a zesty sauce. The label specifies tomato, spinach, pumpkin seeds, white balsamic vinegar, onions, jalapeño, cilantro, chili powder, and cumin.

Bowl: 2 medium sweet potatoes, about 1 lb (450 g), peeled and cut into ¾-inch cubes
¾ cup dry tri-color quinoa, rinsed
1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
½ small yellow onion, finely diced
Estimated cilantro–white balsamic dressi: ½ jalapeño, seeded for less heat

steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss sweet potato with 1 tbsp oil, chili powder, ½ tsp cumin, ½ tsp salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet and roast 25–30 minutes, turning halfway, until browned and tender in the center.
Bring quinoa and 1½ cups water to a boil. Cover, reduce heat, and simmer about 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Rest off heat 5 minutes, then fluff.
Heat remaining 1 tbsp bowl oil in a small skillet. Soften yellow onion for 4–5 minutes. Add beans and 2 tbsp water and cook 3–4 minutes until warm and most liquid has evaporated.
Toast pumpkin seeds in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for 2–4 minutes, stirring until fragrant. Remove from the pan immediately.

Blend dressing ingredients until cilantro and jalapeño are finely chopped. Taste and adjust vinegar, salt, or water for a bright, pourable sauce. Its identity and proportions are inferred from the label.

For a chilled bowl like the delivered meal, spread cooked components in shallow containers and refrigerate promptly until cool. Divide spinach among four bowls, then add quinoa, sweet potato, beans, tomatoes, and red onion. Spoon on dressing and finish with pumpkin seeds. You may also assemble with freshly cooked warm components for a home variation.
notes: The page does not identify the zesty sauce by name or supply a formula. The cilantro–white balsamic dressing is a proposed reconstruction based on the listed ingredients.
reheat: The delivered bowl’s instructions call for removing packaging and adding sauce, with no heating step.

basis: The page names Yukon potatoes, chickpeas, sauerkraut, kale, green beans, fresh herbs, lemon-mustard dressing, and toasted pumpkin and sunflower seeds. The title says Dijon; the ingredient label specifies whole grain mustard.

Salad: 1 lb (450 g) Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into ¾-inch pieces
1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
1 cup sauerkraut, drained but not squeezed completely dry
6 oz (170 g) green beans, trimmed and cut into bite-size pieces
2 cups finely chopped kale, tough stems removed
¼ cup finely diced red onion
¼ cup chopped parsley
2 tbsp chopped dill
1 tsp olive oil for softening kale
Salt for potato water
Lemon-mustard dressing: ¼ cup extra virgin olive oil
Salt to taste, after mixing with sauerkraut

steps: Cover potatoes with cold, lightly salted water in a saucepan. Bring to a gentle boil and cook for 10–14 minutes, until a knife slides in easily but the pieces hold their shape. Drain well and spread on a tray to release steam.

Meanwhile, boil green beans in a separate pan for 3–4 minutes until bright and crisp-tender. Transfer to ice water, then drain and pat dry. Massage chopped kale with 1 tsp olive oil for 1–2 minutes to soften it.

Whisk together dressing oil, lemon juice, mustard, granulated garlic, and pepper. Toss the still-warm potatoes with 2 tbsp of the dressing so they take on some flavor. Refrigerate in a shallow container until chilled.
Toast pumpkin and sunflower seeds in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for 3–5 minutes, stirring often, until fragrant and lightly golden. Transfer to a plate to cool.

Gently fold chilled potatoes with chickpeas, drained sauerkraut, green beans, kale, red onion, parsley, and dill. Add half of the remaining dressing, taste, and add more as needed. Check salt only after adding the sauerkraut and mustard.
Serve cold with the seed mixture sprinkled on top. Keep any remaining dressing and seeds separate until serving so the salad stays crisp.
notes: Dressing proportions and component amounts are estimated. Whole grain Dijon follows both the title and ingredient label. The source URL identifies a dated inventory listing for October 3, 2026; no numeric product ID was visible in the URL.
reheat: The delivered meal is served cold. The page specifies no heating step.

short: Kale pesto rigatoni with tomatoes & mushrooms
basis: The description identifies roasted kale blended with almonds, lemon, garlic, and basil, tossed with rigatoni and served with roasted cherry tomatoes and mushrooms. Nutritional yeast appears in the ingredient list.

Pasta and roasted vegetables: 1 pint cherry tomatoes, about 10 oz (280 g)
½ tsp fine salt, divided between the vegetables
Roasted kale pesto: 4 packed cups kale leaves, stems removed and leaves torn, about 4 oz (115 g)
1 tsp olive oil for roasting kale
⅓ cup extra virgin olive oil
¼ tsp fine salt, then more to taste
¼ cup water, plus more as needed

steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss mushrooms with 1 tbsp oil, granulated garlic, and ¼ tsp salt. Toss tomatoes with the other tablespoon oil and ¼ tsp salt. Spread them on opposite halves of a large sheet, or separate sheets if crowded. Roast for 20–25 minutes, stirring the mushrooms halfway, until browned and the tomatoes have blistered.

Toss kale with its 1 tsp oil on another tray. Roast for 5–8 minutes, tossing once, just until wilted with a few browned edges. Watch closely and remove it before it becomes brittle or scorched. Let cool briefly.

Toast almonds in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for 4–6 minutes, stirring, then cool. Pulse almonds and garlic in a food processor until finely chopped. Add roasted kale, basil, lemon juice, nutritional yeast, salt, and ¼ cup water. Process while slowly adding ⅓ cup olive oil, scraping the bowl as needed, to make a thick pesto.
Boil rigatoni in salted water according to its package until al dente. Reserve 1½ cups pasta water before draining.

Return pasta to the warm pot off heat. Add pesto and ½ cup pasta water, then toss thoroughly. Add more pasta water a few tablespoons at a time until the pesto coats the pasta without clumping. Taste and adjust lemon or salt.
Fold in half the roasted vegetables. Divide pasta among bowls and top with the remaining vegetables and their pan juices. Serve immediately.
notes: The source specifies roasted kale, so this reconstruction briefly roasts it before blending. Roast times, quantities, and pesto texture adjustments are estimated. The published 900 calories are for the delivered meal, not a serving of this home version.
reheat: For the delivered meal: remove the film and heat at 350°F for 12–15 minutes, or microwave with vented film for 2–3 minutes. Stir halfway and add a spoonful of water if the pasta seems dry.

short: Sun-dried tomato pesto rigatoni & Brussels sprouts
basis: The page describes almond pesto made with sun-dried tomatoes, basil, garlic, and olive oil, tossed with rigatoni and paired with deeply roasted Brussels sprouts. Lemon, nutritional yeast, and parsley also appear in the label.

Pasta and Brussels sprouts: 1 lb (450 g) Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved; quarter large ones
Sun-dried tomato almond pesto: ¾ cup drained oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, about 4 oz (115 g)
⅓ cup extra virgin olive oil
¼ cup warm water, plus more as needed
¼ tsp fine salt, only if needed after tasting

steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss Brussels sprouts with 2 tbsp oil and ½ tsp salt. Arrange cut-side down on a large baking sheet with space between pieces. Roast for 22–30 minutes until the cut sides are deeply browned and the centers tender. Turn any loose leaves early if they darken too quickly.

Toast almonds in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for 4–6 minutes, stirring frequently. Let cool. If using dry-packed tomatoes instead of oil-packed, soak them in hot water for 15 minutes and drain before measuring.

Pulse almonds and garlic in a food processor until finely chopped. Add sun-dried tomatoes, basil, lemon juice, nutritional yeast, and ¼ cup warm water. Process while drizzling in ⅓ cup oil. Scrape down the bowl and blend to a textured paste. Taste before adding salt; tomatoes may already be salty.
Cook rigatoni in salted water according to the package until al dente. Reserve 1½ cups pasta water before draining.
Off heat, toss pasta with pesto and ½ cup pasta water. Add more pasta water a little at a time until the sauce is glossy and clings to the rigatoni. Taste for salt and lemon.
Divide among bowls and sprinkle with parsley. Serve Brussels sprouts alongside or on top just before eating to preserve their crisp edges.
notes: The label does not identify whether the sun-dried tomatoes are oil-packed; that is a home choice. It lists sulphur dioxide and sulphites as allergens in addition to almonds and wheat. Unrelated customer reviews on the page were excluded from recipe development.
reheat: For the delivered meal: heat with film removed at 350°F for 12–15 minutes, or microwave with vented film for 2–3 minutes. Stir halfway and add a spoonful of water if dry.

basis: The page describes fusilli in vegan cheese sauce with spicy vegan chorizo chili, Parmesan-style breadcrumbs, and pico de gallo. The ingredient label includes potato, carrot, nutritional yeast, cornstarch, vegan cheddar, and both Impossible meat and vegan chorizo.

Pasta and cheese sauce: 1 medium potato, peeled and diced, about 6 oz (170 g)
1 medium carrot, peeled and thinly sliced, about 3 oz (85 g)
½ tsp each garlic powder and onion powder
¼ tsp fine salt, then more to taste
¾ cup reserved vegetable cooking water, plus more to thin
Chorizo chili: ½ cup cooked black beans, drained
Salt and black pepper to taste
Pico de gallo: ¼ serrano pepper, minced, optional for more heat

steps: Heat oven to 375°F. Cover potato and carrot with water in a saucepan and simmer 12–15 minutes until very tender. Reserve at least 1½ cups cooking water, then drain the vegetables.

For the chili, heat 1 tsp oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook onion 5 minutes, then add ground meat substitute and chorizo. Crumble and cook through according to their package directions. Add garlic, tomato paste, chipotle, cumin, and oregano; stir 1 minute. Add tomatoes and beans, then simmer uncovered 8–10 minutes until thick. Taste for salt and pepper.

Blend cooked potato and carrot with ¾ cup reserved cooking water, nutritional yeast, lemon juice, sauce oil, cornstarch, garlic and onion powders, paprika, and ¼ tsp salt. Return to the saucepan and gently simmer, stirring, for 2 minutes so the cornstarch thickens. Add vegan cheddar and stir over low heat until melted. Thin with reserved cooking water as needed; it should pour easily, since baking thickens it further.

Cook fusilli in salted water for 2 minutes less than the package’s al dente time. Drain, retaining ½ cup pasta water. Toss with cheese sauce, then fold in the chili. If the mixture seems tight, add a little pasta water. Transfer to a roughly 2½-quart baking dish.
Mix panko, vegan Parmesan, and topping oil. Scatter over the pasta. Bake uncovered for 15–20 minutes until hot throughout and the crumbs are golden. Keep an eye on the topping near the end.
Meanwhile, combine pico ingredients and let stand 10 minutes; drain excess liquid. Rest baked pasta for 5 minutes, then serve with pico on the side or spooned over each portion.
notes: The potato-carrot sauce is inferred from the ingredients; CookUnity does not publish its sauce formula or the ratio of the two meat substitutes. These are generous home portions, not replicas of the delivered 383 g portion. Ingredient amounts and baking instructions are untested estimates.
reheat: For the delivered meal: remove the condiment cups, add the breadcrumb topping, and heat with film removed at 350°F for 12–15 minutes. Alternatively add crumbs and microwave with vented film for 3–4 minutes. Add pico de gallo after heating.

short: Griddled veggie chimichangas with roasted potatoes
yield_: 4 servings · 4 burritos with potatoes and dip
basis: The page describes griddled burritos filled with refried black beans, corn, roasted red pepper, white onion, and cheddar, served with roasted red potatoes and avocado aioli. The label also includes lemon, mayonnaise, garlic, taco seasoning, and Italian herbs.

Chimichangas: 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
¾ cup corn, drained or thawed
¾ cup jarred roasted red peppers, drained, patted dry, and diced
1 tbsp neutral oil for filling, plus 2 tsp for griddling
Roasted potatoes: 1 lb (450 g) red potatoes, cut into ¾-inch pieces
Avocado aioli: 2 tbsp water, plus more to thin

steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss potato pieces with their oil, Italian herbs, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet and roast 25–35 minutes, turning halfway, until browned and tender.

Heat 1 tbsp filling oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook onion for 5–7 minutes until soft. Add minced garlic and taco seasoning, stirring for 30 seconds. Add beans and ¼ cup water; simmer 3–5 minutes while mashing most of the beans to make a thick spread.

Fold in corn and well-drained roasted peppers. Cook for 2–3 minutes until excess moisture evaporates. Taste before salting, since taco seasoning may contain salt. Remove from heat and let cool for 5 minutes.
Blend avocado, mayonnaise, lemon juice, grated garlic, and 2 tbsp water until smooth. Add more water a teaspoon at a time if needed to make a dip. Taste and adjust salt.

Warm tortillas briefly in a dry skillet or under a damp towel in the microwave until flexible. Divide filling among them, keeping it in the lower center and leaving a wide border. Add ¼ cup cheddar to each. Fold the sides inward, bring the lower edge over the filling, and roll snugly to enclose.

Brush a large skillet with the remaining 2 tsp oil. Cook burritos in batches over medium-low heat, seam-side down first, for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and the cheese melts. If browning before the center is hot, lower the heat and cover briefly. Serve with roasted potatoes and avocado aioli.
notes: The home method follows the description’s griddled preparation. Mayonnaise and cheddar make this a vegetarian recipe with egg and dairy, rather than vegan. Quantities, seasonings, and sauce ratios are estimated.
reheat: For the delivered meal: reserve the sauce cup. Heat with film removed at 350°F for 12–15 minutes, or microwave with vented film for 2–3 minutes. Serve the sauce as a dip.
